claim_verdicts.evidence: OrderService.cs:8 `public async Task<Order> PlaceOrderAsync(int customerId, List<OrderItem> items)`; :10 `if (items.Count == 0) throw new ArgumentException("an order needs at least one item");`; :12-18 `new Order { CustomerId = customerId, PlacedAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow, Status = "new", Items = items }`; :19 `await repository.AddAsync(order);` :20 `await repository.SaveChangesAsync();` :21 `notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed");` :22 `return order;`. Both code blocks match lines 6-23 and 29-38 character-for-character.

OrderService.cs:31-32 `var order = await repository.FindAsync(orderId) ?? throw new KeyNotFoundException($"order {orderId} not found");` :34 `order.Status = "cancelled";` :35 `await repository.SaveChangesAsync();` :36 `notifier.Send(order.Id, "order cancelled");` :37 `return order;`.

ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs: `catch (KeyNotFoundException ex) { ... WriteProblemAsync(context, StatusCodes.Status404NotFound, "Not found", ex.Message); }` then `catch (ArgumentException ex) { ... StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest ... }`. Registered first in the pipeline: Program.cs `app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>();`.

OrderServiceTests.cs `PlaceOrderAsync_NoItems_Throws`: `var service = new OrderService(new FakeOrderRepository(), new FakeNotifier()); await Assert.ThrowsAsync<ArgumentException>(() => service.PlaceOrderAsync(customerId: 1, items: []));`. No ASP.NET Core type in the file (usings: DonHang.Domain, Xunit). Note: the test also constructs FakeOrderRepository and FakeNotifier — see issue on section 4.

OrderService.cs has exactly two public methods, PlaceOrderAsync and CancelOrderAsync; its only types are Order, OrderItem, IOrderRepository, INotifier, ArgumentException, KeyNotFoundException, DateTimeOffset. DonHang.Domain.csproj is `Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk"` with no PackageReference/ProjectReference, so no ASP.NET Core or EF Core type is reachable.

OrdersController.cs:21 `int.Parse(User.FindFirstValue(JwtRegisteredClaimNames.Sub)!)`; :58-63 `private static OrderDto ToDto(Order order) => new(...)`. OrderService.cs:10 empty-items throw, :16 `Status = "new"`, :21 `notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed")`. Try-it expected answer (1,4 controller; 2,3,5 service) matches.

Design principle, restating the glossary definition of service-layer ("taking and returning plain data with no HTTP involved") that the lesson defines in section 3; not a versioned behaviour. Consistent with the repo: PlaceOrderAsync/CancelOrderAsync take int/List<OrderItem>, return Order, and throw BCL exceptions.

Follows from the premise: if the parameter were an HTTP request type, every call site must supply one. "token included" in section 6 holds because the customer id currently comes from the token's `sub` (OrdersController.cs:21), so a request-taking service would read it from there.
